Commands using `get_formatter().format_issues()` (Family A)\n55\t\n56\tFour commands route `&[Issue]` through the shared `JsonFormatter`. Commands using custom `println!` serialization (Family B)\n95\t\n96\tTen commands serialize non-`Issue` data inline. This is largely **justified**: the `Formatter`\n97\ttrait is keyed to `&Issue`/`&[Issue]` and has no method for `Stats`, `VelocityStats`, `Event`,\n98\tbatch results, claim results, or dependency trees. They fall into three serialization styles:\n99\t\n100\t**`to_string_pretty(&T)` on a `Serialize` struct** (struct field order, 2-space indent):\n101\t- `stats` → `Stats` object (`:2589`)\n102\t- `velocity` → `Vec<VelocityStats>` array (`:2862`)\n103\t- `log` → `Vec<Event>` array via `crate::log::format_events_json()` (`src/log.rs:142-144`, called at `:3070`)\n104\t- `labels` → `Vec<String>` array (`:2495`)\n105\t- `mitosis` → `Vec<BatchResult>` array (`:2224`)\n106\t- `critical-path` → `CriticalPath` object with nested `beads[]` (`:3101`)\n107\t- `schema` → `Issue` object or `{\"schema\": SQL}` (`:2674`/`:2677`/`:2644`)\n108\t\n109\t**`serde_json::json!({...})` literal → `Display`/`to_string_pretty`** (keys **sorted\n110\talphabetically**, see §4):\n111\t- `claim` → single result object, hand-picked projection (`:1755`/`:1799`/`:1838`/`:1866`/`:1907`)\n112\t- `dep tree` → object with `nodes[]` (`:2398`/`:2408`)\n113\t- `schema` `\"all\"` target → `{\"schema\": SQL}` (`:2641`)\n114\t\n115\t**`to_string(&vec![out])` compact** (struct field order, single line):\n116\t- `show` → single-element array `[{…}]` (`:1464`) — array-wrapped for NEEDLE compatibility\n117\t\n118\t### `claim` detail (carried from bf-2x0p, still accurate)\n119\t\n120\t`claim` bypasses the formatter because it emits a **single** hand-picked projection mixing\n121\tfields from `ScoredBead`, `ClaimResult`, and the caller's `assignee`/`workspace` — not an\n122\t`Issue`, and not a struct's `Serialize`. Four mutually exclusive branches (dry-run / any /\n123\tfallback-any / normal) each emit a different object shape; every branch emits at least\n124\t`bead_id` + `assignee`, and every branch's empty/no-candidate case emits the literal `{}` via\n125\t`println!(\"{{}}\")` (`:1777`/`:1817`/`:1884`/`:1920`). Always a single object, never an array.\n126\t\n127\t---\n128\t\n129\t## 4. Inconsistencies in array / object formatting\n130\t\n131\tAfter `ready`'s migration, the old headline inconsistency (list/search JSONL vs. ready array)\n132\tis gone. What remains:\n133\t\n134\t1. **Container shape for \"list of beads\" is JSONL, but `show` is a 1-element array, and\n135\t   `ready`'s empty case is `[]`.**\n136\t   - `list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`(non-empty) → JSONL (no array, no `[…]`)\n137\t   - `ready` (empty) → `[]`\n138\t   - `show` → always `[{…}]` (even though it is logically a single bead)\n139\t   - The remaining list-style commands that *do* use arrays (`velocity`, `log`, `mitosis`,\n140\t     `labels`) emit arrays of non-`Issue` rows, so the JSONL-vs-array split is now strictly\n141\t     \"Issue lists = JSONL, everything else = array.\" That is a defensible rule, but it is\n142\t     **undocumented** and breaks the reasonable expectation that `--format json` yields a\n143\t     parseable JSON document (JSONL is not a single JSON value).\n144\t\n145\t2. **Empty-case handling differs across list-style commands.**\n146\t   - `list`/`search`/`recent` → *no output at all* (empty string). A consumer reading stdout\n147\t     gets `EOF`/parse error, not `[]`.\n148\t   - `ready` → `[]`\n149\t   - `claim` → `{}` (single-object shape; appropriate)\n150\t   - `velocity`/`log`/`mitosis`/`labels` → `[]`\n151\t   - `stats`/`critical-path`/`dep tree` → always emit a full object (never truly \"empty\")\n152\t\n153\t3. **Compact vs. pretty printing.**\n154\t   - Compact (`to_string` / JSONL): `list`, `search`, `recent`, `ready`, `show`, `claim`\n155\t   - Pretty (`to_string_pretty`, 2-space indent): `stats`, `velocity`, `log`, `dep tree`,\n156\t     `labels`, `schema`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`\n157\t   - No command lets the user choose; it is hard-coded per command.\n158\t\n159\t4. **Trailing newline.**\n160\t   - Family A uses `print!` (the only newlines are the JSONL separators; no trailing newline\n161\t     after the last object).\n162\t   - Family B uses `println!` (trailing newline).\n163\t   - A consumer doing `bf search --format json | jq` is fine, but byte-for-byte stable\n164\t     consumers notice.\n165\t\n166\t5. **Key ordering.**\n167\t   - Struct-`Serialize` (`list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`/`show`, `stats`, `velocity`, `log`,\n168\t     `labels`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`) → **struct declaration order**.\n169\t   - `json!` macro (`claim`, `dep tree`, `schema` `\"all\"`) → **alphabetical**. `serde_json`\n170\t     in `Cargo.toml` does **not** enable `preserve_order`, so `json!` builds a `BTreeMap`-backed\n171\t     `Map` and `Value::Display` sorts keys. (Empirically verified for `claim` in bf-2x0p.)\n172\t   - Harmless to generic-object parsers; differs byte-for-byte.\n173\t\n174\t---\n175\t\n176\t## 5. Notable defects / surprises\n177\t\n178\t1. **⚠ `stats --format json` + any breakdown flag emits invalid combined output** (bf-20da,\n179\t   still present). The `--by-type` / `--by-priority` / `--by-assignee` / `--by-label` blocks\n180\t   (`src/cli/mod.rs:2599-2630`) run *after* the format match and always use plain `println!`\n181\t   text regardless of `--format`. So `bf stats --format json --by-type` prints the JSON object\n182\t   **followed by** un-ignorable text (\"By type: …\"). The combined stdout is not valid JSON.\n183\t   **Fix:** when `format == \"json\"`, fold breakdowns into the object as nested maps\n184\t   (`by_type`/`by_priority`/…) instead of printing text.\n185\t\n186\t2. **`show` wraps a single bead in an array** (`:1464`). Intentional and now documented in a\n187\t   code comment: NEEDLE's `parse_single_bead` expects `Vec<Bead>` and takes the first element.\n188\t   Surprising for a user expecting a bare object, but correct for the NEEDLE contract. **Action:\n189\t   surface this in `--help` / README**, not change the behavior.\n190\t\n191\t3. **`ready`'s `[]` empty case diverges from its JSONL siblings.** Minor, but it means\n192\t   `bf ready --format json` on an empty board yields a valid JSON value while `bf list --format\n193\t   json` on an empty board yields an empty string. Either make `list`/`search`/`recent` emit\n194\t   `[]` on empty, or drop `ready`'s special case.\n195\t\n196\t---\n197\t\n198\t## 6. The `JsonFormatter` itself\n199\t\n200\t**Location:** `src/format/json.rs:17-29` (trait + `get_formatter` in `src/format/mod.rs`).\n201\t\n202\t```rust\n203\tfn format_issues(&self, issues: &[Issue]) -> String {\n204\t    issues\n205\t        .iter()\n206\t        .map(|issue| {\n207\t            let mut stripped = issue.clone();\n208\t            stripped.dependencies = vec![];\n209\t            stripped.comments = vec![];\n210\t            serde_json::to_string(&stripped)\n211\t        })\n212\t        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()\n213\t        .unwrap_or_default()\n214\t        .join(\"\\n\")\n215\t}\n216\t```\n217\t\n218\tBehavior worth recording:\n219\t- Returns **JSONL**, not a JSON array.\n220\t- **Strips `dependencies` and `comments`** before serializing (br/NEEDLE compatibility).\n221\t- Empty input → `\"\"` (no output) — because `.join(\"\\n\")` on an empty vec is empty.\n222\t- Compact objects; key order = `Issue` struct field order.\n223\t- `format_issue` (singular) and `format_error` exist on the trait but are **not called** by any\n224\t  command's JSON path (verified: the only `format_*` call sites are the four `format_issues()`\n225\t  uses in §2).\n226\t\n227\t`OutputFormat` also has `Toon` (text-art) and `Text` variants; `ToonFormatter`/`TextFormatter`\n228\tshare the trait. `velocity` is the only command with an explicit `\"toon\"` arm beyond `\"json\"`.\n229\t\n230\t---\n231\t\n232\t## 7. Recommendations for standardization\n233\t\n234\tListed roughly in order of value-to-effort.\n235\t\n236\t1. **Decide and document the JSONL-vs-array rule.** The de-facto rule is already coherent —\n237\t   *Issue lists emit JSONL; all other structured output emits a JSON value* — but it is\n238\t   unwritten. Either (a) document it prominently (README + per-command `--help`) and accept\n239\t   JSONL, or (b) standardize on **real JSON arrays** by giving `JsonFormatter` a\n240\t   `format_issues_array()` (or a `--json-mode array|jsonl` flag). JSONL is the more surprising\n241\t   choice for `--format json` consumers; option (b) is the cleaner long-term target but is a\n242\t   **breaking change** for any consumer that today splits `list`/`search` output on newlines.\n243\t\n244\t2. **Standardize the empty case for list-style commands.** Pick one: either all Issue-list\n245\t   commands emit `[]` on empty (change `format_issues` to return `[]` for empty input, which\n246\t   also subsumes `ready`'s special case), or none do. Today's split (ready → `[]`, others →\n247\t   nothing) is the worst of both. Cheapest win in the audit.\n248\t\n249\t3. **Fix the `stats` breakdown defect (§5.1).** This is a real correctness bug, not a style\n250\t   choice: `--format json --by-*` produces non-JSON stdout. Fold breakdowns into the object as\n251\t   nested maps when `format == \"json\"`.\n252\t\n253\t4. **Standardize compact-vs-pretty.** Either pretty-print everything (more readable, what most\n254\t   \"pretty\" CLIs do) or add `--pretty`/`--compact`. The current per-command split is arbitrary.\n255\t\n256\t5. **Standardize trailing newline.** Trivial: route Family A through `println!` (or document\n257\t   that list commands emit no trailing newline). Aligns byte-for-byte output across commands.\n258\t\n259\t6. **Document the `show` array-wrap contract** (`§5.2`) in user-facing docs so NEEDLE\n260\t   compatibility is visible rather than surprising.\n261\t\n262\t7. **(Optional) Enable `serde_json` `preserve_order`** if byte-stable key order for `claim`/\n263\t   `dep tree`/`schema` matters; otherwise leave as-is (alphabetical is deterministic).\n264\t\n265\t### Non-recommendations (leave alone)\n266\t\n267\t- Family B commands that bypass the formatter are **correct to do so** — they serialize\n268\t  non-`Issue` data the trait was never designed for. Forcing them through a formatter would\n269\t  require a trait method per data type (`format_stats`, `format_velocity`, …) with no\n270\t  cross-format benefit. The split in §1 is the right architecture; only the *output shape*\n271\t  conventions need harmonizing (recs 1–5), not the routing.\n272\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8b5dd199-15f1-4db4-9762-c06ca7d98bb0","uuid":"b1660490-27b9-4e36-bb29-29179a728ba4","timestamp":"2026-07-22T15:35:51.303Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/coding/bead-forge/src/json_formatter_audit.md","content":"# JSON Output Audit — Consolidated Summary\n\n**Consolidating beads:** bf-xmwq (original comprehensive audit), bf-5haf (`list`/`ready`),\nbf-2x0p (`search`/`claim`), bf-20da (`stats`/`velocity`), bf-4w48 (this consolidation)\n**Date:** 2026-07-22\n**Scope:** Every `bf` subcommand that accepts `--format json` (i.e. exposes a `format` field\nin the `Commands` enum).\n**Method:** Findings below are verified against the **current** source (`src/cli/mod.rs` — 3325\nlines, `src/format/*.rs`, `src/log.rs`, `src/velocity.rs`, `src/storage/sqlite.rs`) and, where\nnoted, the live `target/debug/bf` binary. They fall into three serialization styles:\n\n**`to_string_pretty(&T)` on a `Serialize` struct** (struct field order, 2-space indent):\n- `stats` → `Stats` object (`:2589`)\n- `velocity` → `Vec<VelocityStats>` array (`:2862`)\n- `log` → `Vec<Event>` array via `crate::log::format_events_json()` (`src/log.rs:142-144`, called at `:3070`)\n- `labels` → `Vec<String>` array (`:2495`)\n- `mitosis` → `Vec<BatchResult>` array (`:2224`)\n- `critical-path` → `CriticalPath` object with nested `beads[]` (`:3101`)\n- `schema` → `Issue` object or `{\"schema\": SQL}` (`:2674`/`:2677`/`:2644`)\n\n**`serde_json::json!({...})` literal → `Display`/`to_string_pretty`** (keys **sorted\nalphabetically**, see §4):\n- `claim` → single result object, hand-picked projection (`:1755`/`:1799`/`:1838`/`:1866`/`:1907`)\n- `dep tree` → object with `nodes[]` (`:2398`/`:2408`)\n- `schema` `\"all\"` target → `{\"schema\": SQL}` (`:2641`)\n\n**`to_string(&vec![out])` compact** (struct field order, single line):\n- `show` → single-element array `[{…}]` (`:1464`) — array-wrapped for NEEDLE compatibility\n\n### `claim` detail (carried from bf-2x0p, still accurate)\n\n`claim` bypasses the formatter because it emits a **single** hand-picked projection mixing\nfields from `ScoredBead`, `ClaimResult`, and the caller's `assignee`/`workspace` — not an\n`Issue`, and not a struct's `Serialize`. Four mutually exclusive branches (dry-run / any /\nfallback-any / normal) each emit a different object shape; every branch emits at least\n`bead_id` + `assignee`, and every branch's empty/no-candidate case emits the literal `{}` via\n`println!(\"{{}}\")` (`:1777`/`:1817`/`:1884`/`:1920`). Always a single object, never an array.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Inconsistencies in array / object formatting\n\nAfter `ready`'s migration, the old headline inconsistency (list/search JSONL vs. ready array)\nis gone. What remains:\n\n1. **Container shape for \"list of beads\" is JSONL, but `show` is a 1-element array, and\n   `ready`'s empty case is `[]`.**\n   - `list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`(non-empty) → JSONL (no array, no `[…]`)\n   - `ready` (empty) → `[]`\n   - `show` → always `[{…}]` (even though it is logically a single bead)\n   - The remaining list-style commands that *do* use arrays (`velocity`, `log`, `mitosis`,\n     `labels`) emit arrays of non-`Issue` rows, so the JSONL-vs-array split is now strictly\n     \"Issue lists = JSONL, everything else = array.\" That is a defensible rule, but it is\n     **undocumented** and breaks the reasonable expectation that `--format json` yields a\n     parseable JSON document (JSONL is not a single JSON value).\n\n2. **Empty-case handling differs across list-style commands.**\n   - `list`/`search`/`recent` → *no output at all* (empty string). A consumer reading stdout\n     gets `EOF`/parse error, not `[]`.\n   - `ready` → `[]`\n   - `claim` → `{}` (single-object shape; appropriate)\n   - `velocity`/`log`/`mitosis`/`labels` → `[]`\n   - `stats`/`critical-path`/`dep tree` → always emit a full object (never truly \"empty\")\n\n3. **Compact vs. pretty printing.**\n   - Compact (`to_string` / JSONL): `list`, `search`, `recent`, `ready`, `show`, `claim`\n   - Pretty (`to_string_pretty`, 2-space indent): `stats`, `velocity`, `log`, `dep tree`,\n     `labels`, `schema`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`\n   - No command lets the user choose; it is hard-coded per command.\n\n4. **Trailing newline.**\n   - Family A uses `print!` (the only newlines are the JSONL separators; no trailing newline\n     after the last object).\n   - Family B uses `println!` (trailing newline).\n   - A consumer doing `bf search --format json | jq` is fine, but byte-for-byte stable\n     consumers notice.\n\n5. **Key ordering.**\n   - Struct-`Serialize` (`list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`/`show`, `stats`, `velocity`, `log`,\n     `labels`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`) → **struct declaration order**.\n   - `json!` macro (`claim`, `dep tree`, `schema` `\"all\"`) → **alphabetical**. `serde_json`\n     in `Cargo.toml` does **not** enable `preserve_order`, so `json!` builds a `BTreeMap`-backed\n     `Map` and `Value::Display` sorts keys. (Empirically verified for `claim` in bf-2x0p.)\n   - Harmless to generic-object parsers; differs byte-for-byte.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Notable defects / surprises\n\n1. **⚠ `stats --format json` + any breakdown flag emits invalid combined output** (bf-20da,\n   still present). The `--by-type` / `--by-priority` / `--by-assignee` / `--by-label` blocks\n   (`src/cli/mod.rs:2599-2630`) run *after* the format match and always use plain `println!`\n   text regardless of `--format`. So `bf stats --format json --by-type` prints the JSON object\n   **followed by** un-ignorable text (\"By type: …\"). The combined stdout is not valid JSON.\n   **Fix:** when `format == \"json\"`, fold breakdowns into the object as nested maps\n   (`by_type`/`by_priority`/…) instead of printing text.\n\n2. **`show` wraps a single bead in an array** (`:1464`). Intentional and now documented in a\n   code comment: NEEDLE's `parse_single_bead` expects `Vec<Bead>` and takes the first element.\n   Surprising for a user expecting a bare object, but correct for the NEEDLE contract. **Action:\n   surface this in `--help` / README**, not change the behavior.\n\n3. **`ready`'s `[]` empty case diverges from its JSONL siblings.** Minor, but it means\n   `bf ready --format json` on an empty board yields a valid JSON value while `bf list --format\n   json` on an empty board yields an empty string. Either make `list`/`search`/`recent` emit\n   `[]` on empty, or drop `ready`'s special case.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The `JsonFormatter` itself\n\n**Location:** `src/format/json.rs:17-29` (trait + `get_formatter` in `src/format/mod.rs`).\n\n```rust\nfn format_issues(&self, issues: &[Issue]) -> String {\n    issues\n        .iter()\n        .map(|issue| {\n            let mut stripped = issue.clone();\n            stripped.dependencies = vec![];\n            stripped.comments = vec![];\n            serde_json::to_string(&stripped)\n        })\n        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()\n        .unwrap_or_default()\n        .join(\"\\n\")\n}\n```\n\nBehavior worth recording:\n- Returns **JSONL**, not a JSON array.\n- **Strips `dependencies` and `comments`** before serializing (br/NEEDLE compatibility).\n- Empty input → `\"\"` (no output) — because `.join(\"\\n\")` on an empty vec is empty.\n- Compact objects; key order = `Issue` struct field order.\n- `format_issue` (singular) and `format_error` exist on the trait but are **not called** by any\n  command's JSON path (verified: the only `format_*` call sites are the four `format_issues()`\n  uses in §2).\n\n`OutputFormat` also has `Toon` (text-art) and `Text` variants; `ToonFormatter`/`TextFormatter`\nshare the trait. `velocity` is the only command with an explicit `\"toon\"` arm beyond `\"json\"`.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Recommendations for standardization\n\nListed roughly in order of value-to-effort.\n\n1. **Decide and document the JSONL-vs-array rule.** The de-facto rule is already coherent —\n   *Issue lists emit JSONL; all other structured output emits a JSON value* — but it is\n   unwritten. Either (a) document it prominently (README + per-command `--help`) and accept\n   JSONL, or (b) standardize on **real JSON arrays** by giving `JsonFormatter` a\n   `format_issues_array()` (or a `--json-mode array|jsonl` flag). JSONL is the more surprising\n   choice for `--format json` consumers; option (b) is the cleaner long-term target but is a\n   **breaking change** for any consumer that today splits `list`/`search` output on newlines.\n\n2. **Standardize the empty case for list-style commands.** Pick one: either all Issue-list\n   commands emit `[]` on empty (change `format_issues` to return `[]` for empty input, which\n   also subsumes `ready`'s special case), or none do. Today's split (ready → `[]`, others →\n   nothing) is the worst of both. Cheapest win in the audit.\n\n3. **Fix the `stats` breakdown defect (§5.1).** This is a real correctness bug, not a style\n   choice: `--format json --by-*` produces non-JSON stdout. Fold breakdowns into the object as\n   nested maps when `format == \"json\"`.\n\n4. **Standardize compact-vs-pretty.** Either pretty-print everything (more readable, what most\n   \"pretty\" CLIs do) or add `--pretty`/`--compact`. The current per-command split is arbitrary.\n\n5. **Standardize trailing newline.** Trivial: route Family A through `println!` (or document\n   that list commands emit no trailing newline). Aligns byte-for-byte output across commands.\n\n6. **Document the `show` array-wrap contract** (`§5.2`) in user-facing docs so NEEDLE\n   compatibility is visible rather than surprising.\n\n7. **(Optional) Enable `serde_json` `preserve_order`** if byte-stable key order for `claim`/\n   `dep tree`/`schema` matters; otherwise leave as-is (alphabetical is deterministic).\n\n### Non-recommendations (leave alone)\n\n- Family B commands that bypass the formatter are **correct to do so** — they serialize\n  non-`Issue` data the trait was never designed for. Forcing them through a formatter would\n  require a trait method per data type (`format_stats`, `format_velocity`, …) with no\n  cross-format benefit. The split in §1 is the right architecture; only the *output shape*\n  conventions need harmonizing (recs 1–5), not the routing.\n","numLines":272,"startLine":1,"totalLines":272}}}
